3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The two ministers left the room. We took a short break before continuing to the second part.

4.speaker: Lucian Galade
4.text: “Gentlemen, thanks for coming to this significant gathering. Let's begin.”

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Iosef made his way towards the table while the others stood by the door.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Upon invitation, Iosef Lancea along with three high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Defense, walked into the room. One of the men was none other than General Kruger, the Chief of the Armed Forces.

8.speaker: Narrator
8.text: He was in his 70s, yet he had a bulky body that was a result of his commando training. Not only was he the second-most-decorated officer in Sordland, he was also the longest serving.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: General Kruger stepped forward and saluted. He had a strong jaw with sharp cheekbones. His tall stature, uniform and medals, combined with his deep and intense stare, made him look threatening.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Iosef tapped his foot impatiently. He seemed uneasy with the presence of another high-ranking officer in the room.

15.speaker: Iosef Lancea
15.text: “Mr. President. The situation at the western and northern borders towards Rumburg is very tense. We are observing deployments of divisions closer to our border.”

16.speaker: Valken Kruger
16.text: “The picture is becoming clearer. The latest information from the Interior about the weapons caches and now there is an active military build-up close to our borders.”

17.speaker: Valken Kruger
17.text: “The entire situation was analysed by our General Staff and our prediction is a future territorial incursion by Rumburg.”

18.speaker: Valken Kruger
18.text: “We will not let you down, Mr. President. The General Staff is composed of the smartest military individuals.”

19.speaker: Player
19.text: “Let them come, we will give them hell.”

20.speaker: Valken Kruger
20.text: “With all due respect, I think you are underestimating what we could face.”

21.speaker: Player
21.text: “I have complete trust in the General Staff.”

22.speaker: Valken Kruger
22.text: “I share your enthusiasm. We draw our strength from the brave sons and daughters of Sordland but we wouldn't be able to stand against them right now.”

24.speaker: Iosef Lancea
24.text: “Rumburg has been acting increasingly expansionist in the past decades and also interfered in Agnolia, but now they have turned their sights on us.”

27.speaker: Player
27.text: ”I trust the capabilities of our armed forces to handle any threats.“

28.speaker: Iosef Lancea
28.text: “I can assure you of our capabilities, but we don't have unlimited resources.”

31.speaker: Iosef Lancea
31.text: “We are observing these areas actively. Our contingency plans are ready.”

32.speaker: Iosef Lancea
32.text: “Patrolling close to the borders with our border force and keeping army reserve divisions near.”

34.speaker: Valken Kruger
34.text: “I require an increase in the military budget to enlist more soldiers. Only then, we can stand strong against our enemies. The enlarged armed forces will hold them at bay.”

35.speaker: Iosef Lancea
35.text: “Valken is right. We do need an increase in the military budget. Although we don't see eye to eye on exactly how to spend the budget, that much we agree on.”

39.speaker: Narrator
39.text: I opened the door. Lucian, Nia and Lileas rose from their seats.

40.speaker: Lileas Graf
40.text: “These ill-behaved thugs make our administration look weak. They're also disrupting the peace in those cities, meaning other issues like emigration."

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: Today's security briefing was arranged in two parts, starting with internal matters and moving on to external matters after a short break.

42.speaker: Lileas Graf
42.text: “Our highest internal threat comes from the estimated 20000-strong Bludish Freedom Front led by the imprisoned Dewlen Arge. They are a banned political organization, now a militant force that is trying to incite racial violence.”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “They make a lot of noise but have little substance. A barking dog doesn't bite.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “Are they supported by our Bludish citizens?”

45.speaker: Player
45.text: “Are they cooperating with any Bludish political organizations?”

46.speaker: Lileas Graf
46.text: “It may seem that way from the outside, but police intelligence shows a real potential for them to become dangerous.”

47.speaker: Lileas Graf
47.text: “To some extent. Luckily they couldn't attract a wide audience of Bluds. But they could potentially attract thousands if anti-Bludish sentiment spreads in Sordland again.”

48.speaker: Lileas Graf
48.text: “We expect that more have been smuggled in. A group of Bluds were caught with these guns at a checkpoint not far away.”

49.speaker: Nia Morgna
49.text: “This is grave news, but we must be careful not to stoke the fires of anti-Bludish sentiment.”

50.speaker: Lileas Graf
50.text: “It is the gang violence that is threatening the Nargis and Agnland regions. Two prominent organized crime families are at war, and the potential for bloodshed is real.”

52.speaker: Player
52.text: “I don't think mere gangs can pose a threat to us.”

53.speaker: Lileas Graf
53.text: “One is known as the Koranelli and the other as the Skinner Cartel. They used to be allies until a recent disagreement. Both are active in the cities of Narbel and Estord.”

54.speaker: Lileas Graf
54.text: “The primary reason is deception and corruption. They infiltrated several government offices and the police. That's how they can evade us.”

55.speaker: Player
55.text: “They are playing with fire. I want them gone. For good.”

56.speaker: Lucian Galade
56.text: “Thank you for the updates, Mrs. Graf, Mrs. Morgna.”

60.speaker: Lileas Graf
60.text: “I have received news this morning that the investigation into the murder of Bernard Circas has concluded.”

61.speaker: Lileas Graf
61.text: “After further investigation and testimonies, we have confirmed the motive and also the events leading up to the shooting.”

62.speaker: Player
62.text: “Please enlighten us. The more we know, the better.”

63.speaker: Player
63.text: “Great news. I am eager to hear about the details.”

64.speaker: Nia Morgna
64.text: “The reports around the country indicate that tensions are rising as we feared.”

67.speaker: Lileas Graf
67.text: “Mr. Rayne, we have done our due diligence, and the funding; operatives and strategy all point to a coup plot.”

68.speaker: Lileas Graf
68.text: “Nearly three decades ago, they funded General Rikard and tried to establish a communist dictatorship in our country. If it was not for Colonel Soll, we would have seen the real crisis.”

69.speaker: Player
69.text: “Our country always had issues, this is a part of our job.”

70.speaker: Lileas Graf
70.text: “A few days prior, members of the Red Youth initiated a violent attack on a Young Sords local leader in Jen. We believe the Young Sords then called for revenge, leading to the death of Mr. Circas.”

71.speaker: Lileas Graf
71.text: “Since he often spoke against the Young Sords and nationalist sentiments in the Assembly, he was a big target. Not to mention his radical communist views.”

72.speaker: Player
72.text: “The Red Youth are clearly to blame since they triggered it.”

73.speaker: Lileas Graf
73.text: “Yes. We've kept it at bay for so long, but it seems that there are now new triggers.”

74.speaker: Lileas Graf
74.text: “It is unfortunate, but it was likely that an incident would happen.”

75.speaker: Lileas Graf
75.text: “They struck first, yes. It was obvious that there would be a retaliation.”

76.speaker: Lileas Graf
76.text: “The investigation revealed a very troubling fact. The funding sources of the Red Youth have a clear link to United Contana.”

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: She took a sip from her glass of water and continued.

78.speaker: Player
78.text: “I also don't want to jump to conclusions immediately. We shouldn't create a crisis with them.”

79.speaker: Player
79.text: “I trust Ms. Graf's judgement. United Contana is clearly trying to expand its influence.”

80.speaker: Lucian Galade
80.text: “This is debatable. But yes, we know what more security and surveillance caused to this country under President Soll.”

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: Lileas handed over the report and pointed at a highlighted section in the document.

84.speaker: Player
84.text: “This is proof that they are meddling in our affairs.”

85.speaker: Lileas Graf
85.text: “That the communist superpower is meddling in our affairs.”

86.speaker: Lucian Galade
86.text: “As we feared, the political atmosphere has worsened.”

87.speaker: Lileas Graf
87.text: “Yes, we have found the cash trail.”

89.speaker: Lileas Graf
89.text: “Several Red Youth members with ties to United Contana have been detained, and the information extracted from them points to a preparation for a communist uprising in Sordland."

90.speaker: Nia Morgna
90.text: “I went over the report in detail. It would be wrong to jump to conclusions about a clear foreign interference yet. United Contana has humanitarian and cultural ties with many countries including Sordland.”

91.speaker: Lucian Galade
91.text: “It isn't unusual for the superpowers to influence other nations but I think this case is a little far-fetched. The left lacks popular support in Sordland.”

92.speaker: Lileas Graf
92.text: “Our police chief Karl Greiser has linked the funding channel to the United Contana Consulate in Benfi.”

93.speaker: Lileas Graf
93.text: “As we all know, the enemies of Sordland are many, but we also have threats inside the country.”

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “As the government we have all the power to deal with any threat.”

96.speaker: Nia Morgna
96.text: “If we give up essential freedoms to purchase temporary security, we deserve neither freedoms nor security.”

97.speaker: Lileas Graf
97.text: “Let's not forget that President Soll, God bless him, brought stability after a long period of bloodshed and chaos. But moving on...”

99.speaker: Lileas Graf
99.text: “Many suspected links exist between the Bludish Freedom Front and the Workers' Party of Bludia, but we don't have concrete proof yet.”

100.speaker: Player
100.text: “It was expected that Rumburg would undermine us, but this is too far.”

101.speaker: Player
101.text: “We need to keep level-headed with Rumburg. They are looking for reasons to take action.”

102.speaker: Lileas Graf
102.text: “I agree, the prospect of arming our population against us is a step too far.”

103.speaker: Lileas Graf
103.text: “They will play dirty while we play nice. It is a battle we will lose.”

104.speaker: Player
104.text: “We can't let anyone meddle with our internal stability.”

105.speaker: Lileas Graf
105.text: “Our security services are doing their best to prevent further attempts.”

106.speaker: Lucian Galade
106.text: “I have my concerns about Rumburg too. We need strong allies to withstand such a superior power. They are our nemesis.”

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: I arrived in front of the doors leading to the Situation Room.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: The Minister of Interior, Lileas Graf and the Minister of Justice and Law, Nia Morgna would join us for the first part, the law enforcement briefing.

113.speaker: Narrator
113.text: Everyone in the room sat down except for Lucian. He put on his glasses and went through the documents in front of him. Shortly after, he raised his head to address the attendees.

114.speaker: Lucian Galade
114.text: “I am assuming everyone has already been over the agenda. We all have busy schedules. So without further ado, I will jump into our first topic.”

115.speaker: Lucian Galade
115.text: “Mr. President. Ladies. We will kick off today's meeting with the internal security briefing.”

117.speaker: Player
117.text: “Can we make any direct correlations between the BFF and Rumburg?”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “They are insignificant. Not worth our attention.”

119.speaker: Lucian Galade
119.text: “I would be careful with underestimating them, sir. They might cause legitimate unrest if this goes on.”

120.speaker: Lucian Galade
120.text: “While I agree it would make Sordland a better place, it will not be easy.”

121.speaker: Lileas Graf
121.text: “Well, this concludes the topics for the internal portion.”

122.speaker: Narrator
122.text: For the second part the Minister of Defense, Iosef Lancea would join with a few high-ranking officials including the Chief of the Armed Forces Valken Kruger.

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: He smiled at the gesture and bowed his head in respect.

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: Iosef and Valken took their seats at the table while the rest of the officers stood by the door.

128.speaker: Iosef Lancea
128.text: “Do not forget that during the election you promised to focus on the military. I expect that word to be kept for the defense of our nation.”

129.speaker: Iosef Lancea
129.text: “During the election you said nothing about focusing on our military. I ask you to reconsider and to increase the military budget. The future and safety of Sordland is in your hands.”

130.speaker: Iosef Lancea
130.text: “That is an understatement. Times are changing and war is coming, Mr. President, whether we like it or not. We must be prepared.”

131.speaker: Player
131.text: “I am a man of my word, Iosef.”

132.speaker: Player
132.text: “As you said times change, Iosef. We will see.”

133.speaker: Iosef Lancea
133.text: “Of course you are and that is why I follow you, Mr. President.”

135.speaker: Player
135.text: “As you said times change, Iosef. We will see.”

136.speaker: Player
136.text: “Maybe you are right. Defense of our nation is more important.”

137.speaker: Player
137.text: “I am a man of my word, Iosef.”

138.speaker: Narrator
138.text: A smile brought a glimmer of hope on Iosef's face.

139.speaker: Iosef Lancea
139.text: “That is a valuable trait, Mr. President. However, it will not help when the enemy armies are invading our cities.”

140.speaker: Iosef Lancea
140.text: “I knew you would understand, Mr. President.”

141.speaker: Iosef Lancea
141.text: “Valken, we should go to the Ministry and get further updates from our branches.”

142.speaker: Narrator
142.text: They saluted and left the room.

143.speaker: Narrator
143.text: Rumburg had decided to close their consulate in Lachaven.

145.speaker: Narrator
145.text: Everyone fell silent when a soldier entered the room and let Iosef Lancea know that a call had come through from the Ministry.

146.speaker: Lileas Graf
146.text: “I shall be honest with you. With our current capabilities, we may not be able to prevent the further arming of separatists while maintaining order in Bergia, Nargis and Agnland.”

147.speaker: Player
147.text: “True but I am not fully convinced that would be the right choice.”

148.speaker: Player
148.text: “These threats seem more direct than a few bribes.”

149.speaker: Player
149.text: “We will stick to that promise, especially in light of all this information.”

154.speaker: Lileas Graf
154.text: “You promised to increase Sordland's security and law enforcement budget. You must keep this promise.”

155.speaker: Lileas Graf
155.text: “If the law enforcement budget isn't increased, I can't be fully responsible for what happens. Our police units are spread thin as is.”

156.speaker: Player
156.text: “You will do your job whatever happens. Don't come to me with excuses.”

157.speaker: Player
157.text: “In light of this information, I might increase the law enforcement budget.”

158.speaker: Lileas Graf
158.text: “We will rid our country from separatists and violent thugs if you support us.”

159.speaker: Lileas Graf
159.text: “If threats from separatists and violent thugs aren't cause for serious concern on your end, I don't know what will be.”

160.speaker: Lileas Graf
160.text: “We will rid our country from separatists and violent thugs if you do so.”

161.speaker: Lileas Graf
161.text: “My job is to keep you fully informed, and this is the reality. My experience and expertise in keeping our country safe from violent thugs can only go so far."

162.speaker: Nia Morgna
162.text: “I wish you would stop using the word 'thugs', Lileas. The real problem is corruption, which is fuelling the gang violence and is very likely the reason why these weapons were smuggled in. A higher budget could help us end that.”

163.speaker: Player
163.text: “Valid points. Corruption is the root of all evil, after all.”

164.speaker: Lileas Graf
164.text: “They are, and they need all the attention they can get from our administration.”

165.speaker: Lileas Graf
165.text: “We can look into corruption once the weapons have been found and the gangs have been beaten.”

166.speaker: Narrator
166.text: Lileas pointed to page three in the report.

167.speaker: Lileas Graf
167.text: “Our intelligence intercepted two crates filled with weapons close to the Rumburg border. They were filled with military-grade KA-74s.”

168.speaker: Lucian Galade
168.text: “Rumburg has been acting aggressively in the region for a long time. I am not surprised that they would attempt to weaponize the Bludish people against us.”

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “Lileas, I trust that you can handle them.”

171.speaker: Nia Morgna
171.text: “We are, but it needs all the attention it can get from our administration.”

172.speaker: Player
172.text: “Your Ministry must tackle the issue with persistence Ms. Morgna.”

173.speaker: Nia Morgna
173.text: “Just like previous administrations, kicking the can down the road... This is what's destroying our institutions.”

174.speaker: Lucian Galade
174.text: “It seems like they want to increase the pressure both externally and internally.”

175.speaker: Valken Kruger
175.text: “Our forces would crumble under a decrease and Rumburg would be much more compelled to exploit our weakness.”

176.speaker: Valken Kruger
176.text: “The only way we can guarantee the national survival is through a more capable military force against Rumburg.”

177.speaker: Valken Kruger
177.text: “Our country hasn't fallen to any invading force for two-hundred years, you cannot let it happen, Mr. President.”

178.speaker: Lucian Galade
178.text: “We should find regional allies like Valgsland or Lespia to deter Rumburg. There are several options on the table.”

179.speaker: Player
179.text: “Rumburg wouldn't attack any nation allied with any superpower.”

180.speaker: Player
180.text: “Sordland must stand on its own two feet and be able to defend itself.”

182.speaker: Valken Kruger
182.text: “We stand strong as we've always done.”

183.speaker: Valken Kruger
183.text: “We have no true friends outside these borders.”

184.speaker: Iosef Lancea
184.text: “They could be considered, but why pander to others when we can solve these issues ourselves?”

186.speaker: Valken Kruger
186.text: “Yes, but what is difference between losing your independence to one or the other?”

187.speaker: Iosef Lancea
187.text: “One shudders at the sacrifices they would require us to make.”

188.speaker: Valken Kruger
188.text: “Understood. Raising military readiness is the first call of action. If there is truly an extraordinary attempt, we will relay it to you immediately and wait for further orders, Mr. President.”

191.speaker: Iosef Lancea
191.text: "I brought General Kruger with me due to the escalation on our borders."

193.speaker: Narrator
193.text: Iosef left the room to answer.

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: A few minutes later he entered the room again. His expression had changed.

195.speaker: Iosef Lancea
195.text: “Mr. President. There has been Rumburgian military activity close to the Narbel border. I just spoke with the local commander.”

196.speaker: Iosef Lancea
196.text: “Thank you, Mr. President. You shall be updated if the situation escalates.”

197.speaker: Player
197.text: “Go and show them the might of the Sordish Armed Forces.”

198.speaker: Iosef Lancea
198.text: “We will. You can be sure of that.”

199.speaker: Player
199.text: “Make sure they know we are observant and ready.”

200.speaker: Valken Kruger
200.text: “'Always watching, always ready' is our motto, sir.”

201.speaker: Narrator
201.text: Rumburg was already testing us and the reports from the Interior indicate interference inside our borders. Communists, Nationalists, Bludish rebels, Rumburg expansionism? What was next?

202.speaker: Narrator
202.text: Sordland had always been a key piece in the chessboard of the global rivalry between Arcasia and United Contana. But in the recent years, there was no such aggression from Rumburg. Not at these levels at least.

204.speaker: Narrator
204.text: All it takes is one tiny spark to start the flames of war.

206.speaker: Lucian Galade
206.text: “What is the status on the Bernard Circas investigation?”

207.speaker: Player
207.text: “Radical? Sordland just lost a great writer. For what?”

208.speaker: Player
208.text: “Remain calm. Make sure not to escalate things further. Nobody wants a war.”

209.speaker: Iosef Lancea
209.text: “We will exercise utmost caution, Mr. President.”

211.speaker: Lileas Graf
211.text: “Not yet but we have suspects that indicate such a correlation.”

212.speaker: Nia Morgna
212.text: “These gangs exist because corruption is so common in our country. They buy our police officers and slip by checkpoints.”

213.speaker: Nia Morgna
213.text: “These gangs exist because corruption is so common in our country. They buy our police officers and slip by checkpoints.”

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: Nia eagerly lifted her hand. I motioned for her to speak.

230.speaker: Narrator
230.text: Lilieas and Nia were openly scowling at each other. Lileas turned back to her notes.

236.speaker: Nia Morgna
236.text: "Unfortunately, Governor Bron is directly causing the tensions to increase with his increasingly anti-Bludish stance."

237.speaker: Lileas Graf
237.text: "The governor of Bergia, Phelix Bron, is already taking the necessary measures to counter the threat."

238.speaker: Nia Morgna
238.text: "He is misusing the powers given to him by Tarquin Soll. The insane authority of the governor is surely a root cause."

239.speaker: Lileas Graf
239.text: "I must remind you Governor Bron is directly responsible for the arrest of Dewlen Arge, the previous leader of the BFF."

240.speaker: Lileas Graf
240.text: "It's true that his methods can be extreme at times, but it was his policies that kept the region peaceful over the last decade."

241.speaker: Lucian Galade
241.text: "It would be very difficult to revoke the special status of Bergia under the current circumstances, Ms. Morgna. The presidents no longer have the authority Tarquin Soll enjoyed."

242.speaker: Nia Morgna
242.text: "For now, yes. But with enough justification for it, it would be possible. Anyway... We will be discussing this at a later time."

243.speaker: Player
243.text: "The discrimination Bergia suffers is maddening. We should find a way to revoke the 'special' status of Bergia one way or another."

244.speaker: Player
244.text: "I'd rather not disturb the status quo while we're facing all these threats."

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "Governor Bron and his special powers deserve credit for the current peace in the region."

246.speaker: Nia Morgna
246.text: "I will do my best, Mr. President."

247.speaker: Lucian Galade
247.text: "I agree. We shouldn't rush anything on such a divisive topic."

248.speaker: Lucian Galade
248.text: "The fact that he is an important USP member also makes him a possible ally."

250.speaker: Nia Morgna
250.text: "What is the second most important threat?"

251.speaker: Player
251.text: "Tell me more about the Special Zone."

253.speaker: Player
253.text: "Bergia has always been the region of chaos and trouble. We must be careful."

254.speaker: Nia Morgna
254.text: "As you know, Bergia was given a special status by Tarquin Soll after the full-scale uprising by the BFF against the Sordish government in '35."

255.speaker: Lileas Graf
255.text: "Those couple years were disastrous for Bergia. Dewlen Arge and the BFF declared war on us, openly attacked our people and occupied entire cities."

256.speaker: Lucian Galade
256.text: "It was a massive uprising but I'd like to point out the longest time they were in control of a city was two weeks. I wouldn't call that an occupation."

257.speaker: Nia Morgna
257.text: "Despite the arrest of Dewlen Arge in '44 and the BFF ceasing its activities, the special status of the region were never revoked."

258.speaker: Nia Morgna
258.text: "Today, the Special Zone of Bergia gives the governor insane amounts of authority. He was in trouble with the law before for not following the central government's authority."

259.speaker: Lileas Graf
259.text: "Unfortunately, Bergia also has its own police forces directly commanded by Governor Bron. They are not part of my ministry and only cooperate when they are forced to do so. This is a problem."

260.speaker: Lileas Graf
260.text: "Even though our forces have the authority to serve in Bergia, the Special Zone leaves the security of Bergia mostly in the hands of the governor. That leaves my hands tied."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "We must reverse this situation. It is absurd that the Ministry of Interior doesn't have full control over Bergia's security."

262.speaker: Lileas Graf
262.text: "I agree. I have some ideas about it already. But we can talk about that at a later time."
